title: Detection of Endotoxin in Nano-formulations Using Limulus Amoebocyte Lysate (LAL) Assays
protocol: Prepare the study sample in LAL grade water.
Adjust the pH using pyrogen-free sodium hydroxide or hydrochloric acid if necessary.
Dilute the study sample with LAL grade water to several concentrations, ensuring the highest dilution does not exceed maximum valid dilution (MVD).
Dilute concentrated sodium hydroxide stock using pyrogen-free LAL reagent water to prepare a 0.1 N working solution.
Dilute concentrated hydrochloric acid stock using pyrogen-free LAL reagent water to prepare a 0.1 N working solution.
Reconstitute the Control Standard Endotoxin (CSE) according to the manufacturer's certificate of analysis.
Reconstitute the LAL reagent according to the manufacturer's certificate of analysis.
Label tubes and add 900 μl of LAL-grade water into each tube.
Add 100 μl of 10 EU/mL CSE solution to prepare calibration standard with concentration of 1EU/mL in the labeled tubes.
Repeat serial 10-fold dilution as described above to prepare three lower calibration standards.
Verify that four calibration standards ranging from 0.001 to 1 EU/mL have been prepared.
Combine 50 μl of the 1 EU/ml CSE solution with 950 μl of LAL-grade water to prepare a quality control at 0.05 EU/mL concentration.
Combine 25 μl of the 1 EU/mL CSE solution and 475 μl of the test nanomaterial at a given dilution to prepare an inhibition/enhancement control at 0.05 EU/mL concentration.
Allow the instrument to warm up by turning it on approximately 30 min in advance.
Set the detection wavelength to 660 nm.
Sign in using the username and password.
Open the software by clicking the corresponding icon on the computer screen.
Select Collect data on the software home screen.
Enter the test ID and data group information into the General tab.
Click the Hardware tab.
Choose the instrument type from a dropdown menu.
Set up the detection wavelength to 660 nm for the LAL turbidity method.
Verify that serial number, system ID, and serial port information appear on the screen.
Click OK.
Click OK one more time to confirm.
Enter the sample ID in the same order as the samples are tested.
Use default buttons to enter the negative control, standard curve, and test samples.
Prepare duplicate tubes for each sample and add 200 µL (test ratio 4:1) or 100 µL (test ratio 1:1) of the negative control into pre-labeled glass tubes.
Add 50 µL (test ratio 4:1) or 100 µL (test ratio 1:1) of LAL reagent to the first test vial, vortex it briefly, and insert it into the test slot in the instrument carousel.
If using a 1:1 ratio, add 100 µL of LAL reagent to the first test vial.
Repeat the procedure for other samples.
Process each sample one at a time.
Turn on the instrument approximately 30 min in advance.
Set up the detection wavelength to 405 nm for turbidity LAL.
Open the software by clicking on the corresponding icon on the computer screen.
Sign in by typing the username and password.
Select Collect data on the software home screen.
Enter test ID and data group information into corresponding space in the General tab.
Click the Hardware tab.
Choose the instrument type from a dropdown menu.
Choose the instrument.
Verify that a serial number, system ID and serial port information appear on the screen.
Click OK.
Click OK one more time to confirm.
Enter the sample ID in the same order the sample is tested.
Use default buttons to enter negative control, standard curve and test samples.
Prepare duplicate tubes for each sample.
Add 200 µL (test ratio 4:1) or 100 µL (test ratio 1:1) of negative control (water), calibration standards, quality control, IEC and test nanoparticles into pre-labeled glass tubes.
Add 50 µL (test ratio 4:1) or 100 µL (test ratio 1:1) of LAL reagent to first test vial.
Vortex the test vial briefly.
Insert the test vial into the test slot in the instrument carousel.
If the 1:1 ratio is used, add 100 µL of LAL reagent.
Repeat the procedure described above for other samples.
Process samples one at a time.
Label as many reaction tubes as needed for test samples.
Aliquot 100 μL of water, controls, or test sample per tube.
Prepare CSE such that the final concentration is equal to 4λ.
Combine 100 μL of standard with 100 μL of water or test sample to achieve a final concentration of 2λ.
Repeat three more times for lambda and half-lambda and quarter-lambda concentrations.
Ensure the temperature in the water bath is 37 °C.
Add 100 μL of lysate per test tube, vortex briefly.
Place the rack with all tubes into the water bath for 1 hour.
Invert each tube with a smooth motion.
Manually record results on the bench sheet using “+” (firm clot) or “-“ (no clot or loose clot).
